sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The dispersive power of a prism ______ on the angle of the prism. (b) By Rayleigh's law the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its ______.
Match: (a) Formation of rainbow — ? (b) Blue colour of sky — ? [interference / diffraction / scattering / dispersion]
State True or False: (a) Angular dispersion for two colours is independent of the angle of the prism. (b) The angular width of the primary rainbow is more than that of the secondary.
questions.answer:
(a) False — angular dispersion (μ_v − μ_r)A grows with A.
(b) False — the primary bow is narrower.

questions.q: State True or False: (a) The phenomenon that shows light is transverse is diffraction. (b) When the sky is seen from a satellite it looks black.
questions.answer:
(a) False — it is polarization.
(b) True — there is no air to scatter light.

questions.q: Complete: a 60° prism has D_m = 30°. (a) (A + D_m)/2 = ______. (b) μ = ______.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are anti-Stokes lines?
questions.answer: In the Raman spectrum, anti-Stokes lines are scattered lines of higher frequency (shorter wavelength) than the incident light. The photon gains energy from a molecule already in an excited vibrational state.

or.q: What is dispersion of light? Would you prefer a small-angled or a large-angled prism to produce dispersion?
or.answer: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its colours because μ varies with wavelength. A large-angled prism, since angular dispersion (μ_v − μ_r)A increases with the angle A.

questions.q: The angle of minimum deviation of a 60° glass prism is 39°. Calculate its refractive index. (sin 49.5° = 0.760)
For a glass prism of μ = √3, the angle of minimum deviation equals the angle of the prism. Find the angle of the prism.
Why do most ordinary gases not show dispersion of white light?
questions.answer: Their refractive index is very close to 1 and almost the same for all colours, so the colours are hardly separated.

questions.q: Which of red and green light scatters more, and why?
questions.answer: Green, because scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴ and green has the shorter wavelength.

questions.q: Name two phenomena based on scattering of light.
questions.answer: (1) The blue colour of the sky. (2) The red colour of the sun at sunrise and sunset. (Also the white colour of clouds.)

or.answer: When monochromatic light is scattered by molecules, the scattered light contains, besides the original frequency, weaker lines of slightly lower and higher frequencies (Stokes and anti-Stokes lines).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is the Raman effect? How is the Raman spectrum produced? Explain Stokes and anti-Stokes lines.
questions.answer:
Raman effect: when monochromatic light is scattered by a transparent substance, the scattered light contains the incident frequency ν plus new weaker frequencies ν ± Δν.
Photons collide inelastically with molecules. A photon giving energy to a molecule leaves with lower frequency — a Stokes line (ν − Δν). A photon taking energy from an excited molecule leaves with higher frequency — an anti-Stokes line (ν + Δν), weaker because few molecules are excited.
Δν matches the molecule's vibrational energy levels.

questions.q: A glass prism of angle 60° and μ = 1.5 is immersed in water (μ = 1.33). Find the angle of minimum deviation. (sin⁻¹ 0.56 = 34.3°)
questions.answer:
Relative index μ' = 1.5/1.33 ≈ 1.128.
sin[(A + D_m)/2] = μ' sin(A/2) = 1.128 × 0.5 = 0.564 ≈ 0.56.
(A + D_m)/2 = 34.3° ⇒ A + D_m = 68.6° ⇒ D_m ≈ 8.6°.
The deviation in water is much less than in air (about 37°).

questions.q: Explain why (i) the sky appears blue from the earth and dark from space and (ii) the sun appears red at sunrise.
questions.answer:
(i) Air molecules scatter sunlight with I ∝ 1/λ⁴, so blue is scattered most and reaches our eyes from all parts of the sky. In space there is no atmosphere to scatter light, so the sky looks dark.
(ii) At sunrise sunlight crosses a long path through the air. Most blue light is scattered away, and the remaining light reaching us is reddish.

questions.q: Write the expression for dispersive power. How does the width of a spectrum depend on (i) dispersive power and (ii) the angle of the prism? Why is flint glass preferred?
questions.answer:
ω = (μ_v − μ_r)/(μ − 1); angular dispersion θ = ωδ = (μ_v − μ_r)A.
(i) The width of the spectrum increases with ω.
(ii) It increases with the prism angle A.
Flint glass has a higher dispersive power than crown glass, so it gives a wider spectrum.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define the angle of minimum deviation. Draw the graph between the angle of deviation and the angle of incidence. A 60° prism has minimum deviation A/2; find μ. Derive μ = sin[(A + D_m)/2]/sin(A/2).
questions.answer:
The angle of minimum deviation is the smallest deviation produced by a prism, when the ray passes through symmetrically (i = e, ray parallel to the base).
Graph: δ falls as i increases, reaches D_m, then rises (U-shaped curve).
Derivation: r₁ + r₂ = A and δ = i + e − A. At minimum deviation r₁ = r₂ = A/2 and i = e = (A + D_m)/2. Snell's law gives μ = sin i/sin r = sin[(A + D_m)/2]/sin(A/2).
For A = 60°, D_m = 30°: μ = sin 45°/sin 30° = √2 ≈ 1.41.

questions.q: A ray of white light splits into its colours on passing through a glass prism but not through a glass slab. Explain with diagrams.
questions.answer:
In a prism the two refracting faces are inclined. Each colour has a different μ, so it is deviated by a different amount and the colours spread out — violet most, red least — forming a spectrum.
In a slab the faces are parallel. Each colour is bent at the first face and bent back equally at the second, so all colours emerge parallel to the incident ray, only slightly displaced. They overlap again and the light looks white.
